Minority students are significantly less likely than their white peers to be identified as disabled and may lack access to special education services
But also many have government services up the ass! Do you think people in rural West Virginia have access to all the services that inner city kids have?

Yes they do. The Bush era "No Child Left Behind" provided a clear incentive for schools to classify as many children as possible as "disabled". In a number of circumstances, an individual school's funding will hinge on student achievement scores which will be enhanced by excluding poor performing students from overall testing results. I can't speak directly on West Virginia but I do have direct experience with an all white school (there are a handful of Latino children but no blacks in attendance at the elementary school where I live). Any (and every child) that could be classified as suitable for special education programs were done so. From the school's point of view, their overall academic performance would be rated higher than if the special education students had been included. The school receives greater funding with higher academic testing scores. This directly translates to greater funding for the school. I don't think that it matters that this area is very poor, with a large number of elderly retirees on fixed incomes raising grandchildren. While housing is relatively cheap, all other expenses (power, water, gas, groceries, etc) pretty much mirror national averages.

IMO, I agree with the thesis of the article. White students that are "trouble maker" students get more effort to be included as "disabled" whereas blacks and minority children that are "trouble makers" seem to be targeted more for expulsion.

If your point was that the current government programs for children with disabilities are wasteful, I would agree. I believe that far too many children have been classified as "learning disabled" based on a diagnosis of ADHD or ADD when the real problem is deficient parenting.

I would agree that "poor" areas of the country have less access to all health services. But this isn't what the article appears to be about. The article was discussing disproportion with classification and not availability to services.
